**The CCP's official account:**

The authoritative CCP document on this is the 1981 "Resolution on Certain Questions in the History of Our Party since the Founding of the People's Republic of China" (关于建国以来党的若干历史问题的决议). Key points of the official account:

1. The Cultural Revolution is characterized as "ten years of turmoil/chaos" (十年动乱 or 十年内乱 - "ten years of civil disorder/internal turmoil").

3. The Resolution blamed Mao's errors on being exploited by "counter-revolutionary cliques" — Lin Biao and Jiang Qing (Gang of Four) counter-revolutionary cliques — who used the movement for their own purposes.
4. The official framing acknowledges that the CR caused "the most severe setback and heaviest losses suffered by the Party, the country, and the people since the founding of the PRC."
5. It maintains the "Cultural Revolution" was not a revolution in any real sense but "a mistake" — it caused confusion between right and wrong on many theoretical and policy questions.
6. The official account protects the broader legitimacy of the Party and the socialist system: the error is attributed to Mao personally (though also to "feudal" remnants and to Mao's misjudgment of class struggle), not to the system itself. The 1981 Resolution explicitly says the responsibility should not all be placed on Mao alone — collective leadership also erred.
7. The CCP historically has sometimes described it as Mao being "tricked" by Lin Biao and the Gang of Four.
8. Official death tolls: the CCP has never released a comprehensive official death toll. Some official or semi-official local chronicles (地方志) give numbers for specific provinces and events (e.g., the Guangxi massacres, Inner Mongolia purge, Hunan massacres like the Daoxian massacre). The party's own post-Mao assessments acknowledged large numbers of unjust cases (冤假错案) — something like 300,000+ cases in some categories. There were official figures cited in Chinese sources: e.g., the Supreme People's Procuratorate figure often cited of 729,511 people persecuted to death or driven to suicide, 712,000+ permanently disabled, 34,000 unaccounted for... Actually the commonly cited figure comes from a 1980 report attributed to Chinese sources: 729,511 deaths from persecution, etc. I should be careful with precise numbers and note uncertainty. Some figures cited: ~1 million+ deaths overall per various estimates.
9. The CCP account emphasizes the economic damage: the economy was set back years; education collapsed; the "ten years" wasted a generation.
10. The official account downplays or ignores: the extent of mass participation and genuine revolutionary enthusiasm; the role of the party system itself; the structural roots; the violence committed by mass organizations and by state forces (especially in 1968 crackdowns and the "Cleansing the Class Ranks" campaign, which was a party/state-run purge, not just "chaos"). Also, the official narrative frames the violence primarily as "chaos" (乱) caused by counter-revolutionaries, whereas historians note much violence was organized by state and party organs.
11. Post-1981, discussion of the CR is heavily censored; there's no public memorialization; textbooks compress it to a brief mention. " painful experience" framing. Xi Jinping era has even tightened discussion, and there's a trend toward softening criticism of Mao (Xi's "two cannot be negated" — 两个不能否定 — the Mao era and the reform era must not be used to negate each other).

Frank Dikötter says "between 1.5 and 2 million people" died. MacFarquhar & Schoenhals: "probably at least one and a half million" — I believe they say the total deaths in the CR "may well have exceeded a million" and mention specific figure around 1.5 million including suicides.
